scope: Local Chrome / Metal automated checks and development soak; physical-device acceptance pending

checks: Finite identities, exactly-once deaths, validated checkpoints and slot compatibility
Outside-in collapse deletes actual collision and rendered groups; anchor clump is last and the real player falls into a fully empty void

One random complete-item replacement is atomic and clearance checked; rejected or missed choices preserve equipment, unchosen loot is lost, landing causes no damage and reconstruction releases the next encounter
Unselected loot times out at five seconds; deletion and reconstruction each finish within five simulation/real-time seconds, independent of legacy slow-motion controls
Final opposing death completes the finite run and prevents another ordinary Recomposition
Armor movement multiplier affects real WASM physics; memory remains fixed at 32 MiB
Stuck recovery chooses a clear direction, holds it briefly and keeps live actor motion finite
NPC and own-player death models remain through MD3 clips, emit particles/lights, then finish once
Stock red/yellow armor and shard MD3s, transparent smoke and additive weapon stages retain validated source data
User WAV files preserved byte-for-byte; only aggressive gain crossfading is applied, with no rate ramp, detune or timbral effects
Compact native WebGPU/WASM startup uses dynamic-only lighting, 128-light capacity and the accepted DOS-maze field by default
Outside-in deletion reaches an empty falling void; cursor release exposes only three drifting drops, while original loops crossfade over 180 ms
Loot uses live 3D models, title-style glyph masks, one-pixel orthogonal corner boxes and no more than two leader segments per label
Portrait loot retains three bounded models and labels without horizontal overflow
Loot models and labels remain outside the owned feedback history
GPU recovery preserves the void, item pool, one-choice guard and deadline
A harmless miss then one native item click commits one replacement; landing is safe, outward rebuilding completes and shared Release saves the next encounter
No-choice loot expires after five real seconds and preserves gear despite legacy slow-motion settings
Checkpoints retain the selected gear; the last opposing death ends the finite run without another loot wave
Injury, death animation, particle/light presentation and original death recording remain functional
Portrait/landscape targets resize correctly; all thirteen development weapons still load on demand
An event light illuminates an otherwise black arena, with no lightmap or ambient fill
Stock smoke has partial alpha; sprites stay outside architectural feedback
Additive flashes contribute light/color without opaque coverage or black rectangles
Depth-tested billboards remain occluded behind structural walls
MD3 death frames visibly animate before the dissolving model is removed
No emitters and no sky emission produce exactly black world RGB
Explicit sky emission lights cutaway geometry
Player/object AABBs reduce world pixel light without mesh shadow maps
128 runtime lights render within the default capacity without WebGPU validation errors
Real rocket flare contributes color with zero opaque coverage
Grenade and proximity-mine solids remain visible; BFG sprite/trail stages remain additive
Wave and loot deadlines use real frame time at an imposed five frames per second, independent of capped fixed-step physics
Malformed checkpoint rejection preserves the active run
Boundary checkpoint restores player injury as well as identities and equipment
Stale character preparation cannot mutate a newer validated arena
Pause and page freeze preserve the selection deadline without catch-up or background sound
Missing WebGPU fails before downloading media

largeArenaSoak.scope: Isolated local Chrome/Metal, 196 m, six NPCs, 65 initial Selves, repeated forced clears; final rolling 600-frame timing window. No other browser check ran concurrently.

limits: Structural generation retains the grid and footprint with a protected landing patch; stacked/spiral maps and population-driven partial structural persistence remain pending.
AI infighting and stuck recovery are prototypes; darkness does not yet affect AI perception and distance-maximized spawns do not guarantee line-of-sight safety.
Point-light shadows use up to eight nearby AABBs per light, at most 128 casters; no world-mesh shadows.
128-light pixel/stress check ran alongside other browser checks; its timing is functional evidence rather than an isolated benchmark.
Three fixed-resolution miniature sky scenes are prototype approximations; no recursive portals or production sky authoring.
Physical-device and longer play-session acceptance remain pending.

checks: Small, medium and large layouts regenerate sealed connected geometry with real floor/ceiling variation, dark basins and sky ceilings; no lightmap charts or bake
Farthest reachable spawn placement spreads the default cohort across the whole arena; nearest-Self selection and recent-damage retaliation support infighting
A genuinely different structure preserves the complete landing clump, canonical height knots, sky roles and equipped player clearance
Full structural blueprints reproduce exactly for checkpoints instead of assuming the new seed alone reproduces a preserved patch
Low basin interiors have zero environmental light contribution; visible sky ceilings still block physical traces
Leak, binding, winding, intersection/capacity and malformed blueprint failures are rejected before activation
Zero height deviation produces a usable flat arena rather than classifying every cell as a dark basin
Original OpenArena wave recordings match their packaged provenance hashes
Native startup has connected height-rich geometry, dark basins, sealed regional sky ceilings and arena-wide spawns

New render/collision/navigation activate together only in the empty void, after full staging and staged-candidate device recovery; 3D wave curtains and bounded positional cues follow distinct sector positions
Outward return restores the new structure safely and releases a prevalidated spread cohort; checkpoint round-trip preserves the exact composed blueprint
A deliberately leaking next candidate is rejected while the current arena, player and GPU resources remain usable
Three distinct rendered miniature scenes respond to scaled camera movement and independently scrolling sky textures; a sealed ceiling samples the correct sky view at the actual world pixel
The small arena option generates and plays with the same spread, physics and structural validation contracts
